title: Mitch Morse: "I'm Super Humbled And Excited" For Bills Radio Network Involvement | One Bills Live
text: All right, back here on One Bills Live, Chris Brown, Steve Tasker on a Wednesday. On a day where we announced 23 new affiliates for the Bills Radio Network. title: AK Stays 🚨 Why the Saints are Better with Kamara | INSTANT REACTION
text: AK's coming back. The Saints and Alvin Kamara are working on finalizing a new deal that would return Alvin back to the Saints for the upcoming season. And frankly, this is something that should happen. He should be on this team. The Saints are a better team with him. He was already under contract. Status was obviously up in the air a little bit. There was some back and forth over the last couple months over how this thing was going to work out. Some stuff with how his contract was restructured with the 50% down roll. Took a little bit of time to get the uh negotiations rolling and going and get discussing a new contract for this upcoming season, but the two sides are coming to a place where they're agreeing on a new value, a lowered value from the uh $11 million that he was due to make, which we kind of knew was always going to happen. And it gives Alvin the opportunity to finish his career in New Orleans, the city that has you know, frankly, means a lot to him. Like he's told us before he didn't want to leave. He wanted to be here for the city. Not necessarily because of you know, the the anything else but the city and the people in the city. And now he gets a chance to potentially, we'll see how it goes beyond the season, but potentially finish his career here or at least finish up his tenure here in a way fitting of a legend. Like a legend should get the opportunity to leave the right way, especially when they can still be productive for the team. This video is presented by Matt Bowers Auto Group. So, yeah, man, this has been a a a long time in the in the works. And for a while, it wasn't clear that it was going to happen. Um it was definitely up in the air, and there was definitely some tension building around it, but I I think it alleviates in a way that it should be alleviated. The Saints obviously made their move to get Travis Etienne in the backfield. And he's obviously going to be the guy that this backfield is built around. He's younger. He costs a lot more money. He's more explosive. I mean, like we've talked about these things quite a bit, but I don't think that your team is better without Alvin on the team. I think that if you get him into a role where he can be specialized and make plays and go out and play in space and get in the right system of runs that that suit his skillset, I think that he can still give you quite a bit to be a very productive running back. There's other guys on this team, Audrick Estime, Devin Neal, Kendre Miller, Ty Chandler, and I think all of them have their place and they have their roles. And I think Kendre still remains an incredibly enticing idea for this team, but you're a better team with Alvin. And that was never more apparent to me than during minicamp when we were out there watching him on the final day of it and they have Ty Chandler split out in the slot. They have him split out at wide receiver positions and they're throwing him the ball out there. And it's just like, why why wouldn't you have Alvin doing those things? You are a better team if Alvin's out there doing those things for you. That that's those are the things that he should be doing at this point in his career. He doesn't have to be your lead back. He shouldn't be the guy you're looking at. I think the line on rushing yards for A chain is 800 yards. Like he shouldn't be the guy if you have A chain on your team that you're looking at to get you 800 rushing yards, but he can be a guy that you're still, you know, trying to get 800 yards out of in various forms and fashions and I think he can still be a guy that gives you that type of production depending on what the role is. Um look, I think the idea that the the Saints have with A chain and why they paid him is that they feel like he can be their first down back and their second down back and their third down back and they can go into tempo and they can speed up and they can do all kinds of different things and they don't have to worry about, well, maybe we don't want this guy in production or protection or maybe maybe this guy that we have running the ball we don't want out here in this spot. Like I don't think you that you have to have those concerns with him and I think he's going to eat the bulk of the snaps and be the player that does all those things for you. But I think in the perfect world, Alvin can fit in different places and do different things. As a rookie, he played 39% of his snaps in split out positions. Last year, it was under 10%. I think that you like you're a better team at the maybe 39's a little bit high, but I think you're a better team if it looks something closer to that than what it did last year, where is everything's in the backfield, you're running the ball all the time with them, you're not getting them out in space. His first contact isn't with a linebacker. You know, I think if you're putting them in situations where he can be out in space and he can he can hit the edges and you can get get him the ball out in these situations, his contact balance can still keep him upright when he's going against defensive backs and when he's going against um linebackers and it's not, you know, the edge rusher or the defensive tackle making first contact on him. That was never the thing that made him incredibly special. Now, I think during the peak of his career, he was a really good between the tackles runner, but I think that if you got him back in something resembling more what it looked like in 2017 when he came into the league and Mark Ingram was more of that traditional featured back type player, I think that you have a chance to still get good mileage out of him. And I think he can still be a really good and productive player. I think the idea that like that he can't help your team is incredibly misguided. I think that he can help your team quite a bit in the right role, in the right place and more importantly, at the right price. Like I think it it's totally justified for the Saints to want to rework this deal and get it to a different place. I I I don't think that's ridiculous. I think you have to be realistic about where someone's at in their career and I think Alvin obviously the willingness to do this is reflective of where he's at in his career and you know, I just think I think that the plan has always been to figure out something else for a long-term future back there, but I think these two guys can fit together really well. Achane has experience sharing a backfield. Bigsby did a lot of stuff in in Jacksonville. Alvin's always been a guy that's willing to share the backfield and I think he I think he likes it. I think he likes the idea of it. You know, a lot of guys don't want to share their carries or share the the the glory or share or share that because it's money and recognition and all that stuff. Like he's just really never been that guy. Like he came into the league sharing the backfield and the closeness between him and Mark, that can't be fake. Like that was a real thing with a with a real vision for it and you know, doing the interviews together and all that stuff. And the very first practice, the only practice that Alvin came back for, he made an effort to spend time walking up the sideline with A. Chan, spend time talking to him, getting to know him. Uh, they're in the locker room talking to each other after practice. Like that none of that's that's fake. Like I don't think there's anything in Alvin that's a glory hog or whatever. I think he's happy to do whatever he's asked to do and he's going to do it. I think A, he wants to win and he I think B, he just wants stuff to make sense. And I think the team has a better shot at winning than it has had in quite a while. And I think if you do things the right way, I think it all is going to make sense and I think as long as those two things come together, he can get behind it and I think he's a guy that that is important to still have on this team. I mean, a lot of leadership has been lost. A lot of leadership has been lost. Like he's from the previous era. He knows how to win. I think you need a couple of those guys around still. I think some of those connections of the past, there's still a place for it. But I think more importantly, for Alvin, for the city, for Saints fans, like if this is it, at least you know it's it. You know that there's one more year of it and there's a going to be a send-off and it can be celebrated the right way. And who knows, maybe Alvin plays for someone next year. Maybe that team is the Saints. But I don't think it should have been cut short. I don't think it would have served the Saints any purpose. I don't think this is just ceremonial either. Like I think he can help your team. So, as long as he can help your team and you can end it the right way, I've said it a million times, man. Like there's things where when you're a fan of sports, like certain stories shouldn't end certain ways and this one shouldn't have ended acrimoniously and it's good to see that it's not going to now. There's a chance for it to end the right way. Saints AK one more season at least. Um, they get a chance to go out the right way and everybody gets a chance to say, if it is bye, they get a chance to say it and I think that's the way it should be. That's the way it always should have been. Guy's an icon. Like he means something to this team. He means something to this city and now everyone gets to know and gets to experience that for one last season. For all your coverage of the Saints, check out neworleans.football.

text: It is quickly getting real. Brock Purdy to Mike Evans. Exciting update for you. It appears that Mike Evans was on hand for Camp Purdy in Nashville last week. Jordan Watkins, another 49ers wide receiver, posted this and yes, I can see both Deebo Samuel Robinson and Mike Evans in the photo. So, 49ers veteran receivers coming out to work with Brock Purdy. I think it's time for people to stop lying about Brock Purdy and the 49ers. We had a garbage top 10 quarterback list come out the other day. Here's where I stand on it. This is the only correct place to stand on it. You are judged by your performance in the NFL and we have objective metrics to measure performance. Guess where Brock Purdy resides when it comes to efficiency ever since he joined this league in 2022. Number one. Five playoff wins. Get out of here with Justin Herbert ahead of Brock Purdy. Anyway, more 49ers truth as we talk about this season, set the table. I have the article up on the San Francisco Standard. There have been some suggestions this off season that the 49ers aren't fully going for it here in 2026. Well, actual facts show that those suggestions couldn't be more misguided. Look at cumulative average per year of contracts on each team's books. The 49ers rank number one in the entire NFL. So, by perhaps the most general spending category there is, the 49ers are spending the most in the league. Now, what's really interesting and I delve into this on the article, is that the 49ers also have the most salary cap room in the entire National Football League, 69 million. So, you wonder, how do those two things work together? How can they spend the most and also have the most salary cap room? As you can see, there is an imbalance here on the left side. It is the 49ers APY spending. You see a lot of blue, especially on the offensive side, and you see uh much more mixed colors on the salary cap side. So, the cap hits are smaller than the actual money that the 49ers have committed to players, and this is by design. What the 49ers have done more aggressively than any other team is they've prorated the cap damage into the future. They're taking advantage of the NFL's rising salary cap. I think their salary cap management, along with that of the Philadelphia Eagles, has been the best in the league, but what it has set up is a chance for the 49ers to spend big this year and also have that salary cap room that gives them flexibility for a potential trade acquisition before the November 10th deadline. We've talked about Max Crosby. We've talked about Jessie Bates the III. We'll see what the 49ers need and where they are once this season begins, but I think that the combination of high spending plus high cap allows the 49ers to truly push all chips into the middle of the table this year based on what they need as the season begins. So, with rookies reporting on Saturday and then veterans coming the week after that to the 49ers facility, I think that you could rest assured that San Francisco is very, very aggressive this season. Now, the most fascinating part of all this, and this ties right into Brock Purdy and that 49ers wide receiver core working out in Nashville, and obviously we're going to see all of the receivers on the field with Purdy, all of them except for Brandon Aiyuk, when the 49ers convene for training camp on July 25th. Look at the spending division for the 49ers entering this 2026 season. 67% of the cumulative APY spending headed to the offensive side of the ball. Only about 32% to the defense. Now, 2 years ago, this was essentially inverted. The 49ers were under 40%, 39% when it came to offensive spending, and the defense, they were spending the second most of any team in the NFL on their defense. Now though, the defense is in the 20s, and the offense is number two behind only Philadelphia. So, there was a marked inflection point in 2025 when Brock Purdy signed his extension for $53 million annually. There was also an inflection point in 2024 after the 2024 season when the 49ers decided to modernize the defense. They cut a lot of those bloated veteran contracts, and they spent their first five picks on defensive players in the 2025 draft. You let the rookie wage scale get to work in that scenario. So, the defense has gotten younger and cheaper, and the 49ers hope faster and hungrier. text: Why are you unafraid? >> I think because I'm so so surrounded by love and I know that my family is so strong and they will be okay. He was strong enough, courageous enough, the character to handle whatever was going to come his way. >> A tug of war of is this the right thing to do? Is this the right time? He was just looking to live life the right way. >> The headlines will be engraved in history. Up close, the impact will be just as transformative. >> The day that he came out was one Jason, and literally the very next day was a totally different Jason. The person who walked into our house wearing what he wanted to wear, being who he wanted to be. >> I chose to come out. There was no scandal or anything. This was like, I feel that I am good enough to play in the NBA, and by the way, I'm gay. >> Collins retired from basketball in 2014, and then began living the life he long imagined, including marrying the man he loved. Then, last August, came a very different challenge. >> When he first got diagnosed, he was scrolling through Wikipedia to find out about glioblastoma and how basically it's a death sentence. I just wanted to make sure that his brother knew that Jason Collins mattered. >> Murray Meadow plays club rugby in Atlanta. There's no telling the number of people and the number of lives he saved from suicide, from depression. Not the outside world, not people being bullies, but just saving people from themselves, from making mistakes, you know? Because he said it's okay. >> Happy pride. >> That to me is the ultimate definition of courage. That I don't care what it costs me, if I can help one person, if I can help two people, it's worth it. If any of us can inspire to be a quarter of the person, the partner, the man, and the teammate that he was, that's what we should all dream to be. >> It is truly an honor to welcome Jarron Collins to the stage to represent his brother Jason, the recipient of the Arthur Ashe Award for >> Wow. I miss my brother. I wish that he was here standing to accept this award. But I find myself honored to be here and accept this award on his behalf. I know that if he were here tonight, he would want to thank some people for their love and support throughout his life. His husband, Bronson. The rest of our family, our mom and dad, my aunt and uncle, my wife, our children, and everyone else in our close circle. All of his teammates, coaches, and friends in the basketball world. The courage he showed and the way he moved in this world truly made him a trailblazer, an inspiration to so many others, and his impact will be remembered. I'm humbled and thankful for the amount of support our family has received these past couple months, and I'm grateful every time people I don't even know come up to me and say how much of a powerful impact my brother's decision to come out impacted their life in a powerful way.
